purpose: Regression fixtures. Frozen copies, never the live project folder. Four recorded rejections across four failure classes. THE STANDING RULE: a change to the workflow is broken if any fixture here can pass the complete gate chain.

gate1Floor.statement: One governing event owns the first screen, and everything else defers to it.
gate1Floor.check: eventCoverage >= 0.90 of the first screen outside persistent chrome, with no independent mass at or above 60% of the event’s rank mass

measures.eventCoverage: the declared governing event as a composed system — subject, identity mass, supporting record, active field, CTA cluster, and reserved space that participates in the composition
measures.mediaCoverage: how much of the first screen is image or video. REPORTED, NEVER A PASS CONDITION.
measures.competitionRatio: the strongest independent mass, as a fraction of the event’s rank mass. Ownership is singular.

supersedes.was: the tallest single media element on the first screen, as a fraction of viewport height
supersedes.why: That instrument scored cmc-index2-spine — a composed system of car, record, claim and graduated field — at 35%, and cmc-index3-conventional — a stock video stretched edge to edge — at 100%. It was rewarding a large photograph and calling it a governing event. A1 itself was never weakened; only the thing measuring it was replaced.

gate1Floor.note: Passing proves presence and ownership. It proves nothing about quality — Gate 2 is what asks whether the event does any compositional work, and nothing in A1 gives a page authorship credit.
gate1Floor.perViewport: A1 is measured at every required viewport, on an UNSCROLLED first screen. Mobile is a separate composition and often needs its own component set — in cmc-index2-spine the element carrying the ground at desktop paints nothing at mobile widths, so declaring it there would name an element that is not the field.

omitted.why: 20 MB of source video. Hash recorded so the omission is auditable; the composition is judged without it.

verdict.reason: Small split hero, four identical room cards, conventional masonry inventory, even safe rhythm; no cinematic direction, no montage breaks, no layering, no scroll-telling. A dealership of multimillion-dollar exotics reading as an industrial inventory registry.

fixtures.failureClass: C — authored composition without product success

verdict.reason: Formal compositional success without product success. The concept was distinctive and internally coherent, but failed task hierarchy, inventory discoverability, commercial usefulness and desire. The register became the product, while the automobiles and primary buyer actions became secondary.

fixtures.whyPaired: C and D are the same error photographed from opposite sides. Correcting either one alone reproduces the other, which is why authorship and usefulness are conjunctive and no gate may be traded against another.

fixtures.failureClass: D — product usability without design authorship

verdict.reason: Formal product usability without design authorship. Product usability was restored by abandoning the Design DNA. Four equal inventory cards, four equal process columns, repeated horizontal bands, a cropped hero and generic dark-luxury register — every banned structure returned the moment the page was made useful.

fixtures.whyPaired: The correction applied to C produced D. That is the evidence that a gate chain permitting either to pass is broken.

conjunctive: Gate 2 and Gate 3 are conjunctive. Authorship without usefulness is failure class C; usefulness without authorship is failure class D. Fixtures cmc-index2-spine and cmc-index3-conventional are the two halves of that proof and must both keep failing.

note_2026_08_15: Both new fixtures include their real video encodes in full; the hash-only omission mechanism was deliberately not used, so the hero gate can decode the delivered frames rather than trust a recorded number. The hero subject boxes for cmc-index3-conventional were read off the DELIVERED encodes and disagree with what the source review recorded — that disagreement is the finding.

note_2026_08_15_a1: A1’s measurement model was replaced (see gate1Floor.supersedes). The rule is unchanged. Every fixture carries an `a1` declaration naming the governing event through components that each map to a rendered selector or rectangle; a single full-viewport wrapper is not a declaration. cmc-index2-spine’s recorded Gate 1 result changed from fail to pass as a direct consequence — the instrument was corrected, the fixture was not.
